subtopics.title: UAE Visit: Strategic Outcomes
subtopics.summary: PM Modi's UAE visit produced agreements and proposals on energy security, LPG supply, shipbuilding and defence, and AI infrastructure. The energy outcomes centre on strategic crude storage and an LPG supply partnership with ADNOC. Investment interest in India's infrastructure sector was also noted.
facts: MoU between Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited and Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) for strategic collaboration.
Proposal to store up to 30 million barrels of ADNOC crude oil in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves.
Discussions on storing crude oil in Fujairah under India's Overseas Strategic Reserve Framework.
IOCL and ADNOC signed a strategic collaboration agreement on LPG supply security; a long-term LPG sale deal between ADNOC Gas and IOCL is a potential deal.
Framework advanced for a Strategic Defence Partnership between India and the UAE.
Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World MoU to establish a Ship Repair Cluster at Vadinar.
Cooperation includes offshore fabrication under the Maritime Development Fund Scheme.
Term sheet signed for setting up 8 Exaflop Super Computing Clusters.
Partnership between C-DAC and G42 under India's AI Mission.
Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and National Infrastructure and Investment Fund to explore investments up to US$1 billion in India's infrastructure sector.

subtopics.title: UAE: Trade, Diaspora and Country Profile
subtopics.summary: India-UAE trade in FY 2025-26 stood at US$100 billion, and the UAE is among India's largest energy suppliers and export destinations. The 2022 CEPA and the UAE's share of India's remittance flows are key economic links. The booklet also profiles the UAE's government and the Kafala sponsorship system.
facts: Trade between India and the UAE in FY 2025-26: US$100 billion.
UAE is India's 2nd largest export destination, after the US.
UAE is India's 3rd largest crude oil source.
UAE is India's 3rd largest supplier of LNG and 2nd largest supplier of LPG.
UAE is the only nation participating in India's Strategic Reserve Programme.
In 2022, India was the first country with which the UAE signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
UAE accounted for 18% of India's remittance flows.
UAE is a federal, elective monarchy of 7 emirates; capital Abu Dhabi; currency dirham.
Kafala system: a sponsorship system in Gulf countries that ties a foreign worker's visa and legal status to an in-country sponsor, typically the employer.
Indian nationals form the largest expatriate community within the UAE.

subtopics.title: Norway, Nordic Group and Sweden
subtopics.summary: PM Modi made the first bilateral visit by an Indian PM to Norway in 43 years and attended the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in Oslo. Ties with Norway were upgraded to a Green Strategic Partnership, and ties with Sweden were elevated to a Strategic Partnership. The core Nordic group has five countries.
facts: PM Modi undertook the first bilateral visit by an Indian PM to Norway in 43 years.
The 3rd India-Nordic Summit was held in Oslo; earlier summits were in Stockholm (2018) and Copenhagen (2022).
India and Norway upgraded ties to a Green Strategic Partnership covering clean energy transition, climate resilience, blue economy and green shipping.
Norway formally joined India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
PM Modi was awarded Norway's highest civilian honour, the Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit.
India-EFTA TEPA was signed in 2024.
Norwegian Sovereign Wealth Fund (GPFG) has invested about USD 28 billion in India.
Core Nordic countries: Denmark, Finland, Iceland (least populous), Norway and Sweden (most populous).
India and Sweden elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership and adopted the India-Sweden Joint Action Plan 2026-2030.
India and Sweden launched LeadIT at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019 and endorsed joint development of SITAC, the India-Sweden Technology and Artificial Intelligence Corridor.

subtopics.title: Italy and Netherlands: Partnerships and Heritage
subtopics.summary: India and Italy upgraded ties to a Special Strategic Partnership, targeting EUR 20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029 and backing the IMEEC corridor. Cooperation with the Netherlands covers semiconductors, water management and the return of 11th-century Chola copper plates. The booklet also places the Afsluitdijk Dam in the Netherlands alongside the proposed Kalpasar Project in Gujarat.
facts: India and Italy upgraded bilateral relations to a Special Strategic Partnership.
India and Italy committed to raising bilateral trade to EUR 20 billion by 2029.
Both nations support IMEEC, which aims to improve trade connectivity, logistics, energy and digital links between Asia and Europe.
2027 is declared the Year of Culture and Tourism between India and Italy, marking 80 years of diplomatic relations.
Italy is India's 4th largest trading partner in the EU.
MoU between Tata Electronics and ASML supports India's semiconductor plant in Dholera, Gujarat.
Leiden University returned 11th-century Chola copper plates (Anaimangalam Copper Plates) to India.
Afsluitdijk Dam: a 32 km long barrier dam in the Netherlands that transformed the saline Zuiderzee inlet into freshwater IJsselmeer Lake.
Kalpasar Project (Gujarat): proposed dam across the Gulf of Khambhat, expected to create the world's largest freshwater reservoir.
Kalpasar objectives: freshwater storage, flood control, climate resilience, irrigation support and regional development.

quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates is one of India's most important partners in energy, trade and defence. In FY 2025-26, bilateral trade between India and the UAE stood at US$100 billion, and the UAE is a major supplier of crude oil, LNG and LPG to India. Recent talks have also covered crude storage at Fujairah under India's Overseas Strategic Reserve Framework. A Strategic Defence Partnership framework has been advanced, and a Ship Repair Cluster is planned at Vadinar through an MoU between Cochin Shipyard Limited and Drydocks World. The UAE's defence cooperation has three components, covering the military, the navy and the air force. Indian nationals form the largest expatriate community in the country. The Kafala system regulates the relationship between employers and migrant workers in several Gulf countries, and it has drawn attention to issues such as non-payment of wages. Artificial intelligence is another area of cooperation, with a term sheet signed for 8 Exaflop Super Computing Clusters. Investment cooperation includes plans by two funds to explore investments of up to US$1 billion in India's infrastructure sector. Both sides have also discussed a long-term LPG sale agreement between ADNOC Gas Limited and IOCL. Relations also include joint cultural initiatives, such as an MoU supporting a maritime heritage complex at Lothal in Gujarat.

quizzes.passage: India and the UAE share an economic relationship that runs from energy to investment. Trade between them reached US$100 billion in FY 2025-26, and the UAE is among India's largest sources of crude oil and gas. Discussions have covered a potential long-term LPG sale agreement between ADNOC Gas Limited and IOCL, while a strategic collaboration links IOCL with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company. Investment cooperation includes plans by two funds to explore investments of up to US$1 billion in India's infrastructure sector. A Strategic Defence Partnership framework has also been advanced, with a Ship Repair Cluster proposed at Vadinar. The UAE uses the Kafala system, which regulates relations between employers and migrant workers in several Gulf countries. Remittances from the Gulf form a significant link between the two economies. Artificial intelligence cooperation is also growing, with a term sheet for 8 Exaflop Super Computing Clusters under India's AI Mission. Maritime and cultural cooperation continues as well, including an MoU for a maritime heritage complex at Lothal, in Gujarat. The UAE is also part of the India-Israel-UAE-USA grouping and BRICS, which the booklet lists under multilateral cooperation. Its cultural presence includes a traditional Hindu stone temple in Abu Dhabi, built by BAPS. Both countries also discuss energy storage, with a proposal to store ADNOC crude oil in India's strategic reserves.

quizzes.passage: Italy and India have built a broad relationship that now covers trade, technology, culture and heritage. The two countries have a joint action plan for 2025 to 2029 that covers defence, the economy, connectivity, science and innovation. Italy has also joined the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuel Alliance, and both countries have backed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEEC). Italy is also part of the India-Italy-Japan trilateral, which focuses on Indo-Pacific security, stability and multilateral cooperation. Italy is an important trading partner for India within the European Union, and its Indian diaspora is the largest in the bloc. The Netherlands is another key partner, serving as a gateway to Europe for Indian business and ranking among the top sources of foreign direct investment. Cooperation with the Netherlands includes water management, climate resilience and sustainable infrastructure. Universities in the Netherlands have partnered with IIT Delhi and IISc for semiconductor research, talent development and advanced technology. Cultural diplomacy has also played a role, as ancient copper plates were returned to India by a Dutch university. Leiden University is among the institutions that returned heritage objects to India. Together, these exchanges show how India's partnerships in Europe combine economic, scientific and cultural goals.

quizzes.passage: Italy and India have raised their relationship to a higher level, with cooperation across trade, defence, science and culture. Both countries back a corridor-linked initiative that seeks to improve trade connectivity, logistics, energy and digital links between Asia and Europe. Italy has also joined the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuel Alliance. Its programme for Indian students links them with internships, skill development and corporate employment. Italy is an important trading partner for India within the European Union. The Netherlands is a gateway to Europe for India and a significant source of investment. Cooperation with the Netherlands covers semiconductors, water management, climate resilience and sustainable infrastructure. Dutch universities have partnered with Indian institutions for semiconductor research and talent development. Heritage links are also part of the relationship, since a Dutch university returned ancient copper plates to India. Cooperation in water management also draws on Dutch experience with a large dam that turned a saltwater inlet into a freshwater lake, and India has its own proposal for a large freshwater storage project. The Netherlands also ranks among India's top sources of foreign direct investment, and Italy is also part of the India-Italy-Japan trilateral, which focuses on Indo-Pacific security and stability.
